This image shows a biographical text about playwright Tony Kushner written in French. The text provides information about Kushner's background, education, and career achievements. It mentions that he was born in 1956 in New York to a Jewish family from Louisiana and studied theater at Columbia University.

The text details Kushner's intellectual influences, including Freud, Marx, and Walter Benjamin, and traces his theatrical career, particularly focusing on his most famous work "Angels in America." It describes how the play was first commissioned in 1987 by Oskar Eustis from the Eureka Theatre in San Francisco, and subsequently performed in London, Los Angeles, and New York.

The biography also notes Kushner's other works, including adaptations and screenplays, and mentions his accolades, including the 1993 Pulitzer Prize and Tony Award for "Angels in America." The text is credited to Yannic Mancel and appears to be page 4 of a publication.
